Seven steps · Ajahn Lee, Method 2 3 min · 7 steps
narrated
Ajaan Lee’s seven basic steps: a few long breaths with bud-dho, clear awareness of each breath, finding a comfortable breath and letting it spread from the base of the skull down the spine, legs and a
1. Three (or seven) long breaths: bud on the in-breath, dho on the out, the word as long as the breath.
2. Be clearly aware of each in-and-out breath.
3. Observe the breath: comfortable or not, broad or narrow, fast or slow, short or long, warm or cool.

Bhramari · humming bee breath 3 min · 4 steps
steps only
A soft in-breath, then a long, even hum on the out-breath, with the lips closed, so the vibration fills the skull. Then sit in the silence after the sound.
1. Sit upright, lips closed, teeth slightly apart, jaw soft. Optionally close the ears with the thumbs.
2. Breathe in through the nose.
3. Breathe out slowly with a steady, low hum. Feel it vibrate through the head.
+1 more steps…

Spaciousness · VBT vv. 43–48 3 min · 4 steps
narrated
The spaciousness dhāraṇās of the Vijñāna Bhairava, in Satsang’s words: notice the space of the room, then the space inside the chest, mouth and skull, feel the skin as a thin wall with open space on b
1. Notice the space of the room around you, holding the walls and your body.
2. Sense the space inside the body: the chest, the mouth, the skull.
3. Feel the skin as a thin wall, open space within and without.

Trace the Sound 2.7 min · 5 steps
steps only
A two-minute play. Pick any sound, follow it inward and let it fade on its own. When the line goes flat, rest in what is left. The voice speaks, then stops: the pause is the practice. Repeat it throug
1. Pick a sound that is already here: the room, a fan, traffic, your own breath.
2. Follow it inward until it is only a vibration, not a thing out there.
3. Let it fade the way sounds fade. You are not making it stop.
